name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Decide to adopt the rolling 30-day usage-weighted decay metric for the top 20% of prompts by usage. This balances freshness with stability better than a fixed 7-day decay, catching silent failures without over-rotating prompts that still perform. The trade-off is slightly higher compute cost to recalculate weights daily, but it prevents premature pruning of prompts that dip temporarily but recover.

name: Gauge
text: The rolling 30-day usage-weighted decay risks masking true performance drops by averaging in stale data—if a prompt’s quality dips mid-period, the metric won’t flag it until 30 days later. A better alternative is a hybrid: combine a 7-day hard decay for the top 5% of prompts (to catch fresh regressions) with the 30-day weighted decay for the rest (to stabilize the long tail). Settle it by running both for two weeks and comparing how many silent failures each catches in production.
